segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 1
segments.text: 1. An otherwise valid federal excise tax on the business of selling liquor is not rendered invalid in the particular case by the fact that the business is being conducted in violation of the state law. P. 293.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 2
segments.text: 2. A provision of the Revenue Act of 1926 imposes in addition to the $25 excise tax laid on retail liquor dealers by R. segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 4
segments.text: 13 C, sell v. Benson, supra, 46; Voehl v. Indemnity Insurance Co. 288 U. S. 162, 166.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 5
segments.text: (1) The provision, if regarded as part of the machinery for enforcing the Eighteenth Amendment, fell automatically with the repeal of that Amendment. P. 293.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 6
segments.text: (2) An exaction which in reality is a penalty cannot be converted into a tax by so naming it; its purpose and operation determine its character. P. 294.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 7
segments.text: (3) The additional exaction is not a tax, but a penalty for violation of state law. P. 294.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 8
segments.text: (4) The effect of the exaction in question is, under the guise of a taxing act, to usurp the police powers of the States. P. 296.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 9
segments.text: 3. The United States may not impose penalties for infractions of the criminal laws of a State by her own citizens. P. 296.

segments.label: United States v. Constantine, syllabus ¶ 10
segments.text: 4. The Court has no occasion in this case to consider whether the law in question is, bad for want of the uniformity of operation required by Art. I, § 8 of the Constitution. P. 297.
